If sentiment is >0.67 in the last 3 days and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is <0.33 and forecast is falling, increase forecast by 1.0–2.0% for early horizon (days 1–5) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is 0.00 or negative and forecast is above true value, apply downward correction of 2.0–3.0% in late horizon (days 20–30) to align with bearish sentiment.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 after a low forecast, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in mid-horizon to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
If sentiment is consistently 0.33 or below and forecast is flat, apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias across all horizons to reflect subdued market sentiment.  
If sentiment is >0.67 and forecast is below true value, apply 0.5–1.5% upward bias in late horizon to capture sentiment-driven breakout potential.
